title: Hazard Tree Removal & Flagstone Patio Rebuild
summary: A declining mesquite in a tiled courtyard was cracking the flagstone patio around it. Rather than patch around the problem, we took the tree down in sections, pulled the stump, tore out the damaged flagstone, and relaid the patio on a fresh base.

steps.caption: Rigging the first sections of the declining mesquite before cutting, to control where each piece drops in a tight courtyard.
steps.alt: Crew member climbing a mesquite tree with tag lines rigged before a hazard tree removal in a Las Cruces courtyard

steps.caption: Working the canopy down branch by branch with a pole saw and tag lines, keeping cuts away from the windows and stucco.
steps.alt: Two-person crew removing tree branches with a pole saw and tag line in a Las Cruces courtyard

steps.caption: Down to the stump. The roots had been running under the patio for years — the real reason it needed to come out.
steps.alt: Tree stump cut close to the ground after hazard tree removal on a Las Cruces flagstone patio

steps.caption: With the tree gone, the cracked flagstone it had been heaving for years came out too.
steps.alt: Old flagstone patio demolished into rubble around a fresh-cut tree stump in a Las Cruces courtyard

steps.caption: Fresh flagstone delivered by the pallet for the new patio.
steps.alt: Pallet of new flagstone delivered by flatbed truck for a Las Cruces patio rebuild

steps.caption: Laser level and string lines mark the new patio before the first stone goes down.
steps.alt: Laser level and string lines laying out a new flagstone patio base in a Las Cruces courtyard

note: Reveal photo of the finished patio still needed from David once the new flagstone is set and grouted.
